dress_code.men: Traditional Indian attire: White Dhoti (Pancha) with Angavastram (upper cloth) OR Kurta and Pyjama. (Strictly Prohibited: Western clothes, Jeans, Shorts, T-shirts, Bermudas, Track pants, Lungis, Caps, and Nightwear).
dress_code.women: Traditional Indian attire: Saree, Half-Saree (Langa Voni), or Chudidar / Salwar Kameez with mandatory pinned Dupatta/Chunni. (Strictly Prohibited: Western dresses, Jeans, Tight Leggings without Dupatta, Sleeveless tops, Crop tops, Shorts, and Skirts).
dress_code.foreigners: Must adhere strictly to traditional Indian dress code and sign a faith declaration form at the VQC complex confirming respect for the deity.

electronic_ban.policy: Absolute zero-tolerance ban on all electronic and recording devices inside the temple premises and queue complexes.
prohibited_items: Bluetooth earphones, headphones, and audio recorders
electronic_ban.deposit_facility: Free computerized barcode locker counters available outside VQC I, VQC II, Supatham, and PAC complexes to safely store devices before entering.

dos: Pay obeisance to your Ishta Daivam or Kula Daivam before starting your Tirumala pilgrimage.
Book your travel and accommodation in Tirumala well in advance.
Bathe in the Swami Pushkarini and worship Sri Bhu Varaha Swamy in His temple before worshipping Lord Sri Venkateswara Swamy.
Bathe and wear clean traditional clothes before entering the sanctum shrine of Lord Sri Venkateswara Swamy.
Concentrate on Lord Sri Venkateswara Swamy while inside the temple.
Observe absolute silence and chant 'Om Namo Sri Venkatesaya' inside the temple.
Bathe in the Papavinasanam and Akasha Ganga theerthams in Tirumala.
Respect ancient customs and usages while at Tirumala.
Respect and promote religious sentiments among co-pilgrims.
Deposit all your offerings only into the main Hundi.
Wear a tilak in accordance with your religious affiliation.
Follow the procedures of the temple and wait patiently for your turn for the darshan of the Lord.
donts: Don't come to Tirumala for any purpose other than worshipping the Lord.
Don't carry much jewellery and cash with you.
Don't wear footwear in and around the premises of the temple.
Don't approach touts for accommodation and darshan.
Don't prostrate (sastanga danda pranamam) inside the temple.
Don't throw away the prasadam and teertham given to you at the temple.
Don't eat non-vegetarian food, consume liquor or other intoxicants, or smoke while in Tirumala.
Don't wear any head coverings such as helmets, caps, turbans, and hats inside the temple premises.
Don't commit any act of violence or harshness on the temple premises.
Don't rush in for darshan instead of waiting for your turn in the queue.
Don't enter the temple if, according to custom or usage, you are prohibited from entering.
Don't wear flowers at Tirumala temple, as all flowers of the sacred Seven Hills are reserved for the Lord only.
Don't spit or create a nuisance inside the temple premises.
Don't carry unlicensed weapons or ammunition to Tirumala (licensed weapons/ammunition must be declared at the Alipiri check point with relevant documentation).
